topic: Who remains visible after a neighbourhood improves?
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: Who remains visible after a neighbourhood improves?
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立阅读答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
passage:
A. A fictional redevelopment agency renovated a small shopping street. Two years later, average household income in the surrounding area had risen. The agency used the figure as evidence that existing residents had become better off. A local research group asked whether the same people still lived there. An area can become wealthier because residents prosper, because the population changes, or through a combination of both.

B. The agency had compared two separate household surveys. It had not followed individual households over time. New apartments attracted some higher-income arrivals, while several earlier tenants moved away. Those facts did not establish why every household moved. They did show that a change in the area average could not be interpreted directly as a change for its original residents.

C. The research group proposed a follow-up study of households from the first survey. Keeping contact would require consent, secure records and resources to trace people who changed address. Some would be unreachable. The group planned to report the number lost to follow-up rather than assume that their outcomes matched those of the people who remained in contact.

D. Local businesses presented another mixed picture. New cafes increased the number of premises open in the evening. A long-established repair shop closed after its lease ended. Counting businesses alone would hide this change in services. A wider assessment would describe types of business, opening hours and residents' access to everyday necessities. The group did not propose that every new business was harmful or that every former business should remain indefinitely.

E. The revised evaluation separated changes in place from changes in people's lives. Both mattered, but they required different evidence. Renovated buildings and new activity could be described without claiming that every original household benefited. The agency agreed to publish the population changes beside its income figures. A more cautious account would help readers recognise which benefits were demonstrated and which still needed investigation.

options: Whether household income is ever measurable.

questions.prompt: What was missing from the two surveys?

An assumption that nobody ever moves.

Their incomes will be assumed identical to successful contacts.

questions.prompt: Why is business count alone insufficient?
options: The number of premises never changed.
Residents require only evening cafes.
It can conceal a change in the services available.

answers: It can conceal a change in the services available.

Changes to the area and changes to original residents’ lives.
Old building styles and new paint colours only.
Every new arrival and a proven harmful outcome.
answers: Changes to the area and changes to original residents’ lives.
